title: Characterize which graphs admit robustly acyclic orientations

problemStatement.plain: A finite graph admits a robustly acyclic orientation if and only if it is a cover graph of some poset (Pretzel-Brightwell characterization).
whyMatters: Connects graph orientation theory to partial order theory
Cover graph recognition is NP-complete, showing the problem's intrinsic complexity
Sufficient conditions (bipartite, chi < girth) provide practical criteria

proven: Bipartite graphs always admit robust orientations (proved in Lean)
Bipartite orientation by partition is acyclic and robustly acyclic (proved in Lean)
Cover graph orientation by partial order is well-defined
open: Efficient recognition for specific graph classes beyond bipartite
Tight bounds on minimum chromatic number forcing non-cover-graph at given girth
knownResults.goal: Full characterization via cover graph equivalence with sufficient conditions

approaches.name: Rank-based acyclicity
approaches.description: Model acyclicity via rank functions V -> N rather than walks/paths. This avoids complex walk infrastructure and makes proofs about bipartite orientations trivial.

approaches.name: Bipartite partition orientation
approaches.description: Orient all edges from false-side to true-side. Rank function is side -> {0,1}. Robustness follows because no path can return from true-side to false-side.
